```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

We use `mtcars` (32 cars, 1973–74 models): `mpg` miles per gallon, `wt` weight in
1000 lb, `hp` horsepower, `cyl` number of cylinders, `am` transmission.

```{r data}
mt <- mtcars
mt$am  <- factor(mt$am, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("automatic", "manual"))
mt$cyl <- factor(mt$cyl)
```

## Dummy coding of a factor

A factor with $K$ levels becomes $K-1$ indicator columns (treatment contrasts);
the first level is the baseline.

```{r dummies}
contrasts(mt$cyl)
fit_cyl <- lm(mpg ~ wt + cyl, data = mt)
head(model.matrix(fit_cyl), 4)
coef(summary(fit_cyl))
```

`cyl6 = -4.26`: at the same weight, 6-cylinder cars average 4.26 mpg less than
4-cylinder cars. Change the baseline with `relevel()`; the fit is the same.

```{r relevel}
mt8 <- transform(mt, cyl = relevel(cyl, ref = "8"))
coef(lm(mpg ~ wt + cyl, data = mt8))
all.equal(fitted(fit_cyl), fitted(lm(mpg ~ wt + cyl, data = mt8)))
```

Test the factor as a whole (2 df) with one $F$ test.

```{r factor-test}
anova(lm(mpg ~ wt, data = mt), fit_cyl)
```

## Continuous by factor interaction

```{r am-interaction}
fit_am <- lm(mpg ~ wt * am, data = mt)
coef(summary(fit_am))
b <- coef(fit_am)
c(auto_intercept = b[["(Intercept)"]], auto_slope = b[["wt"]],
  manual_intercept = b[["(Intercept)"]] + b[["ammanual"]],
  manual_slope = b[["wt"]] + b[["wt:ammanual"]])
cross <- -b[["ammanual"]] / b[["wt:ammanual"]]
cross                                        # the lines cross at wt = 2.81
tapply(mt$wt, mt$am, range)                  # observed weights by group
anova(lm(mpg ~ wt + am, data = mt), fit_am)  # F = t^2 for the interaction
```

Manual cars have the higher fitted mpg only for weights below 2.81 (1000 lb);
above that, automatics do. The coefficient `ammanual = 14.88` is the gap at
`wt = 0`, outside the data. Centre `wt` to make it interpretable:

```{r centred}
mt$wt_c <- mt$wt - 3
coef(lm(mpg ~ wt_c * am, data = mt))   # ammanual = gap at 3000 lb
```

## Continuous by continuous interaction

```{r hp-interaction}
fit_hp <- lm(mpg ~ wt * hp, data = mt)
coef(summary(fit_hp))
b2 <- coef(fit_hp)
hp_values <- c(100, 150, 250)
setNames(b2[["wt"]] + b2[["wt:hp"]] * hp_values, paste0("hp=", hp_values))
```

The weight slope is $-8.22 + 0.0278\,\text{hp}$: the positive interaction makes
the weight effect *less* negative as horsepower increases.

## Hierarchical principle: invariance to shifting a predictor

Without the main effect, a shift of the origin changes the model space, hence the fit.

```{r hierarchy}
mt$hp_c <- mt$hp - 150
c(no_linear  = deviance(lm(mpg ~ I(hp^2), data = mt)),
  no_linear_shifted = deviance(lm(mpg ~ I(hp_c^2), data = mt)),
  full = deviance(lm(mpg ~ hp + I(hp^2), data = mt)),
  full_shifted = deviance(lm(mpg ~ hp_c + I(hp_c^2), data = mt)))
c(no_main = deviance(lm(mpg ~ wt + wt:hp, data = mt)),
  no_main_shifted = deviance(lm(mpg ~ wt_c + wt_c:hp, data = mt)),
  full = deviance(lm(mpg ~ wt * hp, data = mt)),
  full_shifted = deviance(lm(mpg ~ wt_c * hp, data = mt)))
```
